Appearance:
MR DHRUV K DAVE(6928) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3,4 MR UTKARSH J DAVE(10620) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR SOAHAM JOSHI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 RAHUL SHARMA(8276) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 ==========================================================

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule returnable forthwith.
Mr. Soaham Joshi, learned APP waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of respondent no.1 - State.
Mr. Rahul Dave, learned advocate waives service not notice of rule for and on behalf of respondent - complainant.

sentences.text: That, after marriage, the complainant started residing with the accused no.1 - husband in joint family at her matrimonial home and after some time, the applicants, out of doubts and suspicions on the complainant, used to taunt the complainant on trivial issues and household works.
That the complainant was subjected to torture and had driven her out of the house and after some time, they brought her back.
That, because of the said torture, the complainant gave an application to the Mahila Police Station,Dahod against the applicants.
Thus, the impugned complaint is filed.

4. Heard learned advocate Mr. Dhruv Dave, learned advocate for the applicants; Mr.
Soaham Joshi, learned APP for the respondent no.1 - State and Mr. Rahul Sharma,
learned advocate for the respondent no.2 - complainant.
5.
Mr. Dhruv Dave, learned advocate for the applicants submits that the applicant no.1 is the father-in-law; applicant no.2 is the mother-in-law of the respondent - complainant.
The applicant no.3 is brother-in-law and residing at United States NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined of America.
The applicant no.4 is the sister-in-law, who residing at Vadodara.
He further submitted that at the time of filing of present application, the applicant no.1 is aged about 65 years and applicant no.2 is aged about 61 years old.

He has submitted that earlier the applicant no.2 has filed a complaint being FIR No.11821030200675 of 2020 on 24.12.2020 before the Jhalod Police Station, Dahod for the offence punishable under Sections-504, 506(2), 427 and 114 of IPC against Akash Pravinbhai Panchal; Dishant Panchal and the complainant viz.Roshniben,
w/o.Hardik Panchal.

He has further submitted that as a counter-blast of that complaint, the present FIR is filed by making false allegations against all the family Rajnikant Kodarlal Panchal vs State Of Gujarat on 9 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121816854/
2 members including the sister-in-law, who is staying at Vadodara since long and brother-in-law who is staying at USA.

sentences.text: He further submitted that the complainant alongwith the accused no.1 - husband is residing separetly at Mumbai after their marriage and the applicants no.1 and 2 are residing at Dahod.
He further submitted that the present applicants have no nexus with the complaint lodged by complainant at Dahod as the complainant had nove resided under one roof with her in-laws.

He further submitted that as per the complaint filed NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined by the complainant, she is staying separately since last almost 21 months and on bare reading of complaint, no offence is made out, which can be believed by this Court at this stage and as no ingredients of Section-498A, 504 and 506(2) of IPC are made out.
He has further submitted that there is no specific allegation against any of the applicants in the FIR.
Therefore, he submits that this Court should exercised its inherent powers under Section-482 of Cr.P.C. by quashing and setting aside the impugned FIR registered against the applicants.

6. Per contra, Mr. Rahul Sharma, learned advocate for the respondent - complainant has submitted that this Court should not exercise power under Section-482 of Cr.P.C. as the complaint is filed by the complainant due to harassment and was not permitted to even enter into matrimonial house.
He further submitted that the ingredients of Section498A, 504 & 506(2) are prima-facie satisfied as the prima-facie case is made out atleast against the applicant nos.1 and 2.
Therefore, he submits that this Court should not exercise its discretion and dismiss the application.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined 7.
Learned APP has also submitted that the accused no.1 - husband is not party to the present application as he has not preferred application.
Accordingly, learned APP submitted that the FIR is clearly disclosed the offence against the present applicants.
He, therefore, submitted that there is no case made out to interfere by exercising powers under Section 482 of the Code as it is a case for trial.
8. I have considered the rival submissions made at the bar.
I have also considered the fact that the applicant no.3 viz.Bhargavkumar Panchal, who happens to be the brother-in- law, is residing at USA and hardly three to four times came in India.
I have also considered the fact that the applicant no.4 is married and residing her matrimonial home at vadodara.
It transpires that there are marital relations between the complainant and the accused no.1 i.e. they are wife and husband and they were residing at Mumbai after the marriage.

9. At this stage, it will be fruitful to mention the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Preeti Gupta & NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined Anr. (supra), wherein it is observed in paragraph 33 thus:-
"33.
The ultimate object of justice is to find out the truth and punish the guilty and protect the innocent.
To find out the truth is a herculean task in majority of these complaints.
The tendency of implicating husband and all his immediate relations is also not uncommon.

At times, even after the conclusion of criminal trial, it is difficult Rajnikant Kodarlal Panchal vs State Of Gujarat on 9 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121816854/
3 to ascertain the real truth.

sentences.text: The courts have to be extremely careful and cautious in dealing with these complaints and must take pragmatic realities into consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases.

The allegations of harassment of husband's close relations who had been living in different cities and never visited or rarely visited the place where the complainant resided would have an entirely different complexion.
The allegations of the complaint are required to be scrutinized with great care and circumspection.
Experience reveals that long and protracted criminal trials lead to rancour, acrimony and bitterness in the relationship amongst the parties.

It is also a matter of common knowledge that in cases filed by the complainant if the husband or the husband's relations had to remain in jail even for a few days, it would ruin the chances of amicable settlement altogether.

The process of suffering is extremely long and painful."
10.

Further, it will also be fruitful to mention the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana V/s Bhajan Lal reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, wherein the Hon'ble NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined Supreme Court has observed thus - "In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Ch.XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Art.226 or the inherent powers under sec.482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

entities.text: State of Haryana V/s Bhajan Lal reported in AIR 1992 SC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under sec.156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of sec.155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined case against the accused.

sentences.text: (4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under sec.156(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."

11. In view of the above and on perusing the contents of the FIR, it appears that the family members of the accused no.1 are unnecessary roped in by the complainant and there are NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3273/2021 ORDER DATED: 09/06/2023 undefined casual references made by her without allegations of active involvement and no specific instances are narrated by the complainant.
No specific details are stated in the FIR.
The allegations against the applicant nos.1 to 4, who are father-in- law, mother-in-law; brother-in-law and sister-in-law, are also general and vague and are bereft of specific instances.

There is no active involvement established of the applicants in meting out cruelty from the contents of the F.I.R.
12.
In this view of the matter, this is a fit case to exercise the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code.
Accordingly, this application is allowed.
The impugned FIR being CR No.11821003210003 registered with Mahila Police Station, District-Dahod, as well as subsequent proceedings, if any,
arising out of the same FIR
are hereby quashed and set aside qua the applicants herein.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
